idiom_name: aiocb + aio_read/aio_write with SIGEV_THREAD or SIGEV_SIGNAL
implementation_notes: The portable POSIX choice (POSIX.1-2001): each operation carries an aiocb whose aio_sigevent names the completion notification (a signal or a spawned notification thread) and whose sival_ptr carries the request token; the dispatcher waits in aio_suspend or runs the notification threads, and the handler harvests results with aio_error and aio_return. glibc implements it in user space with helper threads, so it is convenient but not the fastest engine.
pitfalls: The aiocb and the buffer it points at must not be modified while the operation is in progress and must stay valid until it completes (aio(7)); violating this is silent memory corruption.
The glibc implementation maintains helper threads and scales poorly, as the aio(7) manual itself notes; throughput-sensitive code should use io_uring or the kernel aio syscalls.
A single aiocb may not be reused for simultaneous asynchronous reads or writes; each outstanding operation needs its own control block.

variants.name: Linux io_uring submission and completion rings
variants.idiom_name: io_uring SQ/CQ rings with user_data completion tokens
variants.implementation_notes: True completion-based engine on Linux 5.1 and later: the application fills submission queue entries on a shared ring, submits them with io_uring_enter, and the kernel posts exactly one completion queue entry per request; user_data carries the completion token back, so matching completions to handlers needs no extra bookkeeping. No notification threads are involved and the shared rings avoid copying, which is why it is the modern choice for high-throughput completion-based I/O.
pitfalls: io_uring requests may complete in any order; the completion token in user_data is the only reliable way to map a CQE back to its request.
Errors arrive as a negated errno in the CQE result field rather than through errno; treating res as a byte count unconditionally hides failures.
Overlapping more than one outstanding send or receive on the same stream socket is unsafe (io_uring(7)); ordering must be enforced with links or by issuing one operation at a time.
